card.field: Insurance claims intake and document checks
card.one_liner: Which missing document actually blocks a claim, the 30-day window edge cases, and when to route to appeal.

rules.text: A claim must be filed within 30 days of the incident date.
Every claim needs the incident report, the itemised bill and proof of payment.
A claim on a lapsed policy is declined unless the lapse was under 15 days and the premium was paid in the grace period.
Duplicate claims are checked by policy number, incident date and amount.

exceptions.text: The 30-day window counts from the date the claimant could reasonably know, so a hospital discharge date can replace the admission date.
If only proof of payment is missing and the bill is under 500 dollars, register the claim as pending and give 14 days; do not reject.
A partial approval above 70% of the claimed amount is paid immediately and the remainder goes to review; below 70% the whole claim goes to review.
A lapse of 15 to 30 days with a documented bank failure of autopay is routed to underwriting, not declined.

judgment_calls.text: Two claims with the same incident date but different providers are usually one event, not a duplicate; check the provider before flagging.
A claimant who refiles within 7 days of a decline with the missing document goes to the original handler, not to appeal.
If the itemised bill has a code outside the policy schedule, approve the covered lines and route only the uncovered line to review.

common_mistakes.text: Rejecting for a missing document that is not actually required for claims under 500 dollars.
Flagging same-day claims from two providers as duplicates.
Counting the window from the admission date when the discharge was 10 days later.

never_do.text: Never approve a claim on a policy lapsed more than 30 days; refuse and explain the reinstatement path.
Never route a first refile to appeal; appeal is for a second decline.
Never pay a partial approval without recording which lines were held.
